records.source_role: W3C Recommendation defining testable web accessibility success criteria
records.reporter: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative Accessibility Guidelines Working Group
records.support_role: WCAG 2.2 provides normative success criteria for keyboard accessibility, focus, reflow, text spacing, dragging alternatives, target sizing, time-based media alternatives, and other accessibility outcomes that can support UI rules when the rule stays within the criterion scope.
contraindications: WCAG conformance is scoped to web content and does not by itself prove product usability, native-platform conformance, semantic correctness outside the cited success criterion, or that an automated detector can close the requirement.
records.transfer_boundary: NUI may use WCAG 2.2 to support accessibility rule authority only where the operational contract maps to an applicable success criterion; product-specific behavior, non-web platforms, and evidence sufficiency remain separately adjudicated.

records.source_role: W3C Recommendation defining accessibility semantics and composite-widget requirements
records.reporter: W3C Accessible Rich Internet Applications Working Group
records.support_role: WAI-ARIA 1.2 defines roles, states, properties, ownership relationships, accessible semantics, and focus-management responsibilities for composite widgets including grids and treegrids, giving NUI a primary specification source for semantic table and grid rules.
contraindications: ARIA semantics do not prescribe a product data model, visual layout, persistence architecture, or business workflow; native HTML semantics should be preferred where appropriate and APG interaction examples are guidance rather than automatic conformance proof.
records.transfer_boundary: NUI uses WAI-ARIA only for semantic and focus contracts within ARIA scope. It must not infer that adding an ARIA role repairs an interaction, or that a valid accessibility tree proves the underlying product-state behavior is correct.

records.source_role: NIST final digital identity authentication and authenticator management guideline
records.reporter: NIST authors David Temoshok, Yee-Yin Choong, Andrew Regenscheid, Ryan Galluzzo, James Fenton, Justin Richer, and Naomi Lefkovitz
records.support_role: NIST SP 800-63B-4 defines current technical requirements and recommendations for authentication, authenticator management, assurance, reauthentication, and related digital-identity lifecycle concerns, providing a primary source for identity UI rules when their scope matches the guideline.
contraindications: SP 800-63B-4 is written for digital identity systems, especially government use cases, and does not make every consumer-product authentication preference universal; NUI must preserve assurance-level, threat-model, and jurisdiction context.
records.transfer_boundary: NUI uses the guideline to support authentication and session-management failure boundaries, not to claim blanket legal compliance or to impose a federal assurance requirement on products whose declared risk model does not call for it.

records.source_role: IETF standards-track iCalendar data and scheduling semantics specification
records.reporter: IETF RFC 5545 editor Bernard Desruisseaux and the calendaring standards community
records.support_role: RFC 5545 defines calendar DATE and DATE-TIME values, UTC and local-time forms, time-zone identifiers, recurrence representation, and event scheduling structures, giving NUI a primary source for rules about preserving calendar time semantics across storage, editing, and exchange.
contraindications: RFC 5545 defines an interchange format rather than a complete calendar product UX, so it does not dictate every scheduling interaction, visual representation, or conflict-resolution choice.
records.transfer_boundary: NUI may use RFC 5545 for calendaring semantics that map to the specification but must keep product-level scheduling policy and human-readable presentation as separate operational judgments.

records.source_role: Unicode Technical Standard for locale, number, date, time, and time-zone data
records.reporter: Unicode Consortium CLDR Technical Committee and UTS #35 editors
records.support_role: Unicode UTS #35 and CLDR define stable locale identifiers and data conventions for language, number, currency, date, time, time-zone, collation, and related internationalization behavior that can ground locale-sensitive presentation and parsing rules.
contraindications: CLDR supplies locale data and conventions but does not decide a product's business time zone, accounting policy, scheduling authority, or whether a particular localized label is appropriate for the product domain.
records.transfer_boundary: NUI uses UTS #35 for locale-data and formatting semantics while keeping product policy, source-data truth, and end-user interpretation as distinct verification responsibilities.

records.source_role: W3C Recommendation for geolocation API behavior, privacy, and permission-gated location access
records.reporter: W3C Devices and Sensors Working Group Geolocation specification editors
records.support_role: The W3C Geolocation Recommendation specifies permission-gated access to geographic position and explicitly treats location as privacy-sensitive, supporting UI contracts around permission state, position freshness, accuracy, and truthful handling of unavailable or denied location.
contraindications: The API does not define map visualization, routing quality, geocoding correctness, background-location policy on every native platform, or the precision that a product should promise to users.
records.transfer_boundary: NUI uses the specification for browser geolocation capability and permission truth while keeping map UX, route semantics, native background execution, and domain-specific location accuracy outside the normative claim unless separately evidenced.

records.source_role: W3C Working Draft defining common permission-state infrastructure for powerful web features
records.reporter: W3C Permissions specification editors Marcos Caceres and Mike Taylor with the responsible working group
records.support_role: The Permissions specification documents granted, denied, and prompt-style permission state infrastructure and change observation for powerful features, corroborating UI rules that distinguish requested capability, current permission state, revocation, and feature availability.
contraindications: The document is a Working Draft rather than a final Recommendation, browser implementations differ, and permission state alone does not guarantee the underlying capability will succeed at runtime.
records.transfer_boundary: NUI treats this source as corroboration rather than universal normative authority and requires runtime evidence for actual capability success, failure, revocation, or platform-specific permission behavior.

records.source_role: W3C Candidate Recommendation Draft for camera, microphone, media stream, and device-permission behavior
records.reporter: W3C WebRTC Working Group Media Capture and Streams editors from Cisco, Mozilla, Google, and Apple
records.support_role: Media Capture and Streams defines getUserMedia device access, permission integration, device availability, failure cases, track lifecycle, and privacy-sensitive exposure of media hardware, supporting capture and device-state rules when scoped to observable browser behavior.
contraindications: The specification targets web user agents and does not define every native-camera workflow, document-scanning UX, media-editor lifecycle, or product-specific consent model; it is also a Candidate Recommendation Draft rather than a final Recommendation.
records.transfer_boundary: NUI uses this source as corroborated platform evidence for camera and microphone capability boundaries and still requires product-level verification for capture review, upload authority, native devices, and business workflow semantics.

records.source_role: W3C media accessibility user requirements for controls, captions, descriptions, and alternative access
records.reporter: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative media accessibility task-force contributors
records.support_role: The Media Accessibility User Requirements document identifies accessibility needs for keyboard-operable media controls, captions, descriptions, track selection, playback control, and alternative access, providing strong user-needs evidence for media UI rules beyond a single implementation pattern.
contraindications: This is a user-requirements document rather than a general-purpose product conformance standard, and specific synchronization tolerances or media service policies require separate authority where claimed.
records.transfer_boundary: NUI uses the document as corroborated accessibility evidence and pairs it with WCAG or product-specific runtime evidence instead of treating every listed feature as universally mandatory for every media surface.
